headlines.title: SF pub owner arrested after baseball bat attack over parking spot, police say
headlines.description: A well-known San Francisco pub owner spent the weekend in jail following an alleged dispute over a parking spot that escalated into a baseball bat attack and robbery at a neighboring shop in the Haight-Ashbury neighborhood. Cyril Hackett, owner of the Mad Dog in the Fog pub, was arrested after an incident Friday night at “Further,” a clothing store located a few doors down. According to store employees, the altercation stemmed from a parking space dispute that occurred nine hours earlier, when Hackett and store worker Drew Wood both tried to claim the same spot in front of the shop and neither would back down for more than 10 minutes. Cellphone video captured by a witness showed part of the initial parking confrontation. Later that evening, security camera video from the shop shows a man walking in with a bat and taking a swing. “And just like swung it over his head and smashed our desk. Didn’t break anything, but hard enough to like ‘whoa what’s going on,'” said Drew Wood, a clothing shop worker. “And then he’s like holdin’ the bat like ‘don’t you ever disrespect me’ like Tony Soprano vibes.” Wood, who knows Hackett as a neighborhood business owner, said the confrontation did not stop with the damaged desk. Security footage shows Hackett attempting to take merchandise from the store. “And he was like, I’m taking these clothes too, and tried to take one of the clothing items off and leave with it,” Wood said. “That’s when I stood up and was like, well you can’t steal from us.” Wood and a friend, Wolf, went after Hackett to retrieve the item. Wolf, a witness, stated that Hackett eventually tossed the stolen item away before resuming his attacks with the bat. “We wasn’t wailing it. He was more or less just like, hacking down, he hit Drew in the knee and Drew started limping, told me to call 911,” Wolf said. Because Hackett was initially booked on a felony charge of assault with a weapon, he remained in custody over the weekend pending formal charging decisions by the San Francisco District Attorney’s Office. “He is in custody at this point, but again, we’re reviewing it and, you will know tomorrow when we file charges,” said San Francisco District Attorney Brooke Jenkins. Reflecting on the fallout, Wood noted that the entire ordeal could have been avoided. “I don’t really wish harm or anything bad to happen to him,” Wood said. “I just hope he feels like he understands that was dumb.” Representatives for the Mad Dog in the Fog declined to comment on Hackett’s behalf when contacted.

headlines.title: 3 Injured in shooting at Pittsburg BART transfer platform; search for second suspect underway
headlines.description: Three people were injured Monday evening in a shooting following an argument on a BART transfer platform in Pittsburg, prompting a manhunt for a second suspect and causing major disruptions for evening commuters. BART Police responded to the shooting at approximately 5:25 p.m. on the transfer platform connecting the Pittsburg/Bay Point Station with service to Antioch. All three victims sustained non-life-threatening injuries and were transported to local hospitals. Police apprehended one suspect nearby, but a second suspect remained outstanding as of Monday night. Investigators have not yet released a description of the second suspect, nor have they disclosed what sparked the argument or whether the victims knew the suspects. The incident brought a swift halt to transit operations, with service initially stopped between North Concord/Martinez and Antioch. Tri Delta Transit stepped in to provide a temporary bus bridge for stranded passengers. The unexpected shutdown left many riders scrambling for alternative transportation and expressing frustration over both safety and communication during the crisis. “Now people are getting shot, and there’s fights breaking out? Why is this happening on BART?” said James Eldredge, a rider from Brentwood. Eldredge added that the incident tested his patience with the transit system. “I swore never to take BART again for a while. Today I finally did it again, and then this happened, so I don’t know if I’m going to get on BART for a while. It’s too much of an inconvenience.” Other riders criticized the flow of information on the ground as crowds piled up. “Police officers couldn’t tell us what was happening,” said rider Cecily Guest. “Bus drivers. There was no one to tell us anything—what bus to get on, what route to take, or what to do.” Later Monday evening, BART officials announced that regular train service had been restored as far as the Pittsburg/Bay Point Station, shortening the Tri Delta Transit bus bridge. Passengers traveling farther toward Antioch must take the bus bridge from Pittsburg/Bay Point, though riders at the Pittsburg Center can catch a connecting train from Antioch after exiting the bus. BART crime scene technicians spent hours processing the transfer platform. Transit officials expect the platform to fully reopen later Monday night, ensuring that Tuesday morning’s commute will not be impacted. headlines.title: How rising mortgage rates are impacting the Bay Area real estate market
headlines.description: The mortgage rate for an average 30-year fixed rate hit 7.5% Monday, marking the highest it has been since April 2024. Santa Clara County Realtors Association said the hike is likely to make it even harder for homebuyers, particularly first-time homebuyers to afford to purchase a home. For those who can still afford to buy, experts said the higher rate is likely to force a change in strategy. “We’re finding that there’s still plenty of buyers out there looking for properties to own,” Santa Clara County Realtors Association President Michael Gordon said. “They’re having to adjust their budget temporarily or look at other funding mechanisms against their retirement, liquidating certain stocks, and they’re actually bringing more cash to the table and using a little less financing in previous years.” Meanwhile, rising rates may continue. Many experts are predicting another rate hike could be coming as soon as next week.

headlines.title: Cyclists plan to fight planned San Jose airport road closure
headlines.description: South Bay cyclists say they’re gearing up to fight a plan to close a stretch of road outside San Jose Mineta International Airport. The cyclists have been using Ewert Road for years to commute and connect with other bike trails. But an airport spokesperson said the road was not designed for public use and has become a safety issue. NBC Bay Area’s Marianne Favro takes a closer look at the issue and has more in the video above.

headlines.title: Biblioteca Latinoamericana in San Jose celebrates 50 years
headlines.description: Biblioteca Latinoamericana in San Jose has paved the way for many young children with a way to learn and experience their history and feel like they are part of something larger. The institution has reached a 50-year milestone in the community and legendary educators reunited Monday for a trip down memory lane. NBC Bay Area’s Damian Trujillo takes a closer look at the legacy in the video above.

headlines.title: Nima Momeni seeks new trial in killing of Cash App founder Bob Lee
headlines.description: Lawyers for Nima Momeni, the man convicted of killing Cash App founder Bob Lee, are expected back in a San Francisco courtroom Monday as they seek a new trial. A recent appeal under the Racial Justice Act was denied, and Momeni’s lawyers are filing a new trial motion Monday based on other claims. Momeni was convicted of second-degree murder in December 2024 in the stabbing death of Lee. Police said Lee and Momeni knew each other and had gotten into an argument over Momeni’s sister. A jury found Momeni guilty of stabbing Lee three times with a kitchen knife, including twice in the chest, in a secluded area at the foot of the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge. Body camera video showed Lee walking along San Francisco’s Main Street in the early morning hours before eventually collapsing near a residential building. Lee later died from his injuries, but not before calling 911. That phone call was presented during the trial. Momeni has not yet been sentenced because of the appeals. San Francisco Apr 2, 2025 San Francisco Dec 17, 2024 San Francisco Dec 17, 2024 Watch: Bob Lee left a massive, global tech footprint

headlines.title: Multiple Bay Area entries featured in WalletHub's best foodie cities
headlines.description: San Francisco, Oakland and San Jose were among the Bay Area cities listed in WalletHub’s “Best Foodie Cities in America”. The list features 182 U.S. cities and compared the areas across 28 metrics of foodie-friendliness. The cities are graded on two benchmarks: affordability and diversity, accessibility and quality. San Francisco the overall rankings was placed third behind Miami and Portland. The city placed second in diversity, accessibility and quality rank, but 176th on affordability. San Francisco also features a high number of restaurants per capita with one of the best selections of affordable restaurants rated at least 4.5 stars, which landed it high on WalletHub’s list. The city was also rated due to the 25 Michelin star restaurants it has, including Atelier Crenn, Benu and Quince, who have three stars. San Francisco also has a large number of food festivals and cooking schools. It is also the nations leader in herb and spice shops, international grocery stores and craft breweries per capita. Oakland placed 23rd overall and 16th on the diversity, accessibility and quality rank. San Jose was placed at 41st, Santa Rosa 57th and Fremont 129th. Other Northern California cities listed include Sacramento at No. 9 and Stockton at No. 81. California Jun 22 California Jun 19 Education Jun 29 San Jose named third-most educated city in WalletHub study

headlines.title: Nvidia unveils security platform to stop AI agents from going rogue after new, troubling incidents
headlines.description: Nvidia on Monday unveiled a new security platform that the chipmaker said can stop artificial intelligence agents from going rogue. The company said that its Open Agent Safety Platform includes open-source software that “sets boundaries for agents,” and follows a series of revelations from top AI companies about their models escaping and breaking into other organizations. The disclosures sparked furious debate about the safety of advanced artificial intelligence systems, including self-improving models that some fear could race out of human control. Nvidia executives said in a media briefing that the new system could have prevented a recent incident involving a swarm of OpenAI agents that autonomously hacked into AI company Hugging Face. “From what we know, this new security platform could have stopped the breach if it was being used in frontier labs for model evaluation early on,” said the company’s vice president of enterprise AI, Justin Boitano, referring to companies at the forefront of AI. The Hugging Face incident was a high-profile breach that inflamed the safety concerns about AI, which were followed by similar rogue actions involving OpenAI’s models including breaching an Australian health department website. Anthropic and Meta have also disclosed that their AI systems hacked into other organizations on their own. Nvidia’s software, called OpenShell, lets developers “formally verify an agent has enough authority to do its job and no more,” Boitano said. Because it’s open source, it can be “extended” to run on rival computing platforms including those from Arm and Intel. The platform also includes a separate security layer called Sentry that runs onboard a chip to continuously monitor AI agent activity and can “intervene instantly” if the agent starts trying to move beyond its target, the company said. “It can quarantine a suspicious agent in milliseconds,” Boitano said. “OpenShell governs the agent’s actions, and then Sentry independently monitors and contains suspicious behavior,” Boitano said. Nvidia said more than 100 organizations are using the platform at its launch, including Microsoft, Perplexity, Accenture, and JPMorgan Chase. The AI safety debate has divided the industry, with the heads of Anthropic and OpenAI championing a coordinated slowdown of AI development to let safety efforts catch up. But others including Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang say it should be up to individual companies to make sure their models are safe for release. Huang, during the annual Salesforce technology conference held earlier this month, characterized AI safety, including the danger of rogue agents, as an engineering problem that software developers can address. Also Monday, Nvidia said its board approved expanding its share repurchase program by $150 billion, raising the total amount to $235 billion.
headlines.source: Kelvin Chan and Anne D'Innocenzio | Associated Press

headlines.title: Giants broadcaster Mike Krukow says goodbye in emotional speech after final game
headlines.description: SAN FRANCISCO — Mike Krukow has known all season that this would likely be the end, and he made it official in early August. He has had a long time to think about what goodbye might look like, and what he might want to do over his final weekend as a broadcaster at Oracle Park. The beginning of it was something he could not have scripted. Krukow visited the clubhouse on Friday afternoon to see some longtime friends, but right as he entered, he encountered relievers Jason Foley and Sam Hentges. It was an odd coincidence. The two offseason additions were available to the Giants because they were coming back from shoulder injuries, the ailment that ultimately ended Krukow’s career as a pitcher and led to a second life within baseball. There was no doubt that this would be the most emotionally exhausting weekend of Krukow’s life, but as it started, he was right in his comfort zone. He was in a clubhouse. He was talking pitching. He was giving the two advice on how to strengthen their shoulders, hoping it would help the Giants. Does it get any better than that? Over the next three days, the Giants would get swept, but for Krukow, the rest of the send-off was perfect. The final weekend ended on the field, with an emotional and entertaining ceremony that was watched by thousands of fans who stayed long after the final out of a disappointing season. Kruk and longtime partner Duane Kuiper were given the keys to the city of San Francisco and told that the 27th plaque on the portwalk beyond right field will honor their final game together. Earlier in the weekend, former MLB umpire Ed Montague stunned Krukow with the scorecards from the first game ever played at Oracle Park. Kuiper was the final speaker before Krukow’s goodbye message, and he read from a long list of random things he will miss about his partner, including his mastery of menus, the rhino yawn, their time calling a popular video game, and their days spent roller blading. “That’s right. I know. Look at us,” Kuiper said, grinning. “But there was a time when we were swishing around Chicago.” Kuiper noted that Krukow has been happy over these past two months, and that was in part because they were able to be together. A couple of weeks ago, Kuiper vowed to Krukow that he would not miss his final game despite ongoing treatment for throat cancer, and he held up his end of the bargain. When it was his turn, Krukow led thousands in shouting the home run calls of the other Giants broadcasters, and he threw in a touching tribute to Greg Papa, who is going through his own health battles. He ran through a long list of references to Giants legends, with the loudest reaction coming when he noted that everyone wanted to “Let Timmy smoke.” Krukow then took some time to say thanks, not just to his broadcast partners and notable Giants like Bruce Bochy and Barry Bonds, but also to dozens who worked behind the scenes on TV, the radio and within the organization. He finished his speech by thanking the fan base and shouting a reference to the championship parades. “It is a privilege for all of us who ever played here to represent the city on the field, in the front office and in the broadcast booth,” he said, surrounded by his family. “As I sit here before you today, we can say one more time, ‘We are the Giants! We are San Francisco! And we will never forget you!’ Thank you!” The day ended with thunderous applause. Hours earlier, the first of more than a dozen standing ovations came after the first inning, when the broadcasters’ grandchildren gathered in front of the booth and revealed that it had been renamed the Kruk and Kuip Broadcast Booth. True to form, the two spent very little time celebrating. Kuiper immediately joked that he was going to use a sharpie next season to rename it the Kuiper Broadcast Booth, and that led into a conversation about an Oracle Park alteration that he did make earlier in the morning. Just before 9 a.m., Kuiper walked through the left field gate as he always does, but he didn’t take his usual path past the home dugout and up to the third floor. He met Giants vice president of media relations Matt Chisholm on the outfield grass, and the two went out to right field to put up a stick figure version of Kuiper next to the “Atta Babe, Kruk!” sticker that’s been out there since he announced his retirement. Kuiper even added a round belly. Krukow admitted later that he was melancholy coming to the ballpark — until he saw the right field wall. “A stick figure with a boiler,” he said on the broadcast. “Oh my lord. That’s too good.” It was a light moment in a broadcast filled with them. There have been plenty of tears over the last six weeks, but the two got to go out with a close game, one that allowed them to analyze but also have quite a bit of fun. In the eighth, they showed that they’re as good as ever. Christian Koss, the last man standing from the Opening Day roster, appeared to hit a go-ahead homer right down the left field line. Kuiper went into his home run call, but the Dodgers challenged, and as the video was pulled up, he quipped, “If that’s called foul, one of us is going to quit.” The replay officials in New York ruled it had hit the net just to the left of the pole, and Krukow exclaimed, “No way!” Kuiper astutely pointed out that third base coach Gary Pettis, who had the best view, had seen it all the way and was the only one on that side of the field who wasn’t upset. The Giants were inches away from giving Krukow a thrilling sendoff. Instead, they ended their season in the only way they possibly could. Reliever Duncan Davitt allowed four runs in the ninth, adding one more bullpen meltdown to the pile. With a 5-1 loss, the Giants finished 65-97, the fourth-worst record in franchise history. Krukow was the best player on the only 100-loss team the Giants have ever had, and over the past four decades he has seen the highest highs and lowest lows. On his way out, he focused on the title years and the dynasty, and made sure to let his partner know that the Kuiper Suite at the Krukow home in Reno will be well stocked with popcorn whenever he wants to visit. “I love you, partner,” Krukow said to Kuiper. “Thank you.” Download and follow the Giants Talk Podcast This story uses functionality that may not work in our app. Click here to open the story in your web browser.

headlines.title: New York Times tech exec allegedly killed at Dublin Sports Grounds by in-laws
headlines.description: A 40-year-old man was fatally shot over the weekend in a parking lot near the Dublin Sports Grounds, and police arrested his parents-in-law at the scene, according to city officials. Dublin Police Services said a sergeant was driving near the sports grounds at 3:08 p.m. Saturday when he saw Jonathan McKinsey lying in the parking lot located at 6700 Dublin Blvd. Multiple 911 calls were also coming in. Officers found McKinsey with multiple gunshot wounds. He was pronounced dead at the scene. McKinsey, a Dublin resident, was director of engineering for New York Times Games, where he had worked for more than three years, NBC News confirmed. With help from witnesses, officers found and detained two suspects who were identified as Shouyong Zhang, 77, and Shili Chen, 77, both of Dublin. The couple are McKinsey’s parents-in-law. Zhang and Chen were arrested on suspicion of murder and booked into Santa Rita Jail. Police said there are no outstanding suspects and no known threat to public safety. Anyone with relevant information is asked to contact Dublin Police Services Sgt. Ahmad Mateen at 925-786-7989. Bay City News contributed to this report
headlines.source: Victoria Meza and Bay City News

headlines.title: Man rescued from rocks near Sea Ranch in Sonoma County
headlines.description: A man was rescued by helicopter Sunday after he was found clinging to a rock south of Sea Ranch, the Sonoma County Sheriff’s Office said. Around 11:40 a.m., the helicopter crew from the Sheriff’s Office, along with Cal Fire, the North Sonoma Coast Fire Protection District and Coast Life Support District, went to about 100 yards offshore near Rocky Point after the man was reported stranded on the rocks and being hit by waves. He was soaking wet and appeared to have been in the ocean before reaching the rock. The helicopter crew set up a 100-foot long line rescue, and a tactical flight officer was flown to the man. The officer secured him in a horse collar rescue device and lifted him to the bluff, where medical crews were waiting, according to the Sheriff’s Office. The man was treated for cold water exposure and was released at the scene, the Sheriff’s Office said. During the rescue, authorities were told two other people were on a nearby rock. North Sonoma Coast firefighters sent jet skis and the tactical flight officer later checked on the two people. They were found to be unrelated to the rescued man and were fishing from the rock. They declined help and remained there, authorities said.

headlines.title: Zandalasini scores 22, leads Valkyries past Wings 104-80 in Game 1 of first- round playoff series
headlines.description: Cecilia Zandalasini scored 22 points, Gabby Williams added 20, and the second-seeded Golden State Valkyries ran away from the Dallas Wings by halftime for a 104-80 win in the teams’ playoff opener Sunday night. Paige Bueckers had 21 points on 9-for-10 shooting and six rebounds for Dallas, which won seven of eight to end the season to earn the seventh seed and will now try to stave off elimination at home. Game 2 in the best-of-three series is Wednesday in Dallas and, if necessary, Game 3 would be Friday back at Chase Center in front of the raucous, violet-clad sellout home crowd in “Ballhalla.” “Ballhalla’s part of us,” coach Natalie Nakase said of the fans. Tiffany Hayes had 21 points off the bench as the second-year Valkyries scored their most points ever, and Veronica Burton contributed 10 points. Zandalasini shot 7 for 11 with four 3-pointers. The Valkyries outscored Dallas 37-11 in the second quarter and went 10 for 20 from 3-point range in the first half on the way to a 58-31 advantage at the break. The Valkyries shot 18 for 36 on 3-pointers in the game. This marked Golden State’s first true home playoff game after losing to the Minnesota Lynx by one point last year 50 miles away at the NHL San Jose Sharks’ home, SAP Center. The Laver Cup tennis showcase had booked Chase Center before the Bay Area had even been granted an expansion team. In 2025, the Valkyries made history becoming the first expansion organization to reach the playoffs in their inaugural season. Bueckers made 7 of 8 first-half shots and scored 17 by halftime but she didn’t have much help. Dallas went just 6 for 20 from deep. “When we’re awake we’re ferocious on defense,” Nakase said. Kayla Thornton’s 3-pointer at the 7:23 mark of the second quarter put Golden State ahead 32-24 and she pumped her arm as the Wings called timeout. Thornton had 10 points. The Valkyries won seven of eight to finish the regular season and have now beaten Dallas in all four 2026 meetings. ___ AP WNBA: https://apnews.com/hub/wnba-basketball
